cards.title: Qualifying Allometric Clearance Scaling for Macromolecules
cards.claim: Simple allometry is a candidate for macromolecule clearance when the relevant elimination mechanism is comparable across species. The cited multi-compound evaluation found useful average performance for proteins and peptides, but species-dependent target binding and nonlinear PK produced exceptions. A fixed exponent is a justified scenario choice, not a universal property of all macromolecules.
conditions: The compound is a macromolecule and the dominant elimination mechanism is characterized.
Species binding/activity, dose range and PK linearity are assessed before transfer.
required_inputs: Animal clearance and body weight with parameter basis and uncertainty.
Target body weight, proposed scaling equation and exponent with provenance.
Evidence for comparable elimination mechanisms and target binding across species.
limitations: Molecular size alone does not qualify a scaling method.
A good average result in a reference dataset does not establish target-specific accuracy.
Receptor-mediated elimination or nonlinear PK may require a different bridge or explicit sensitivity scenarios.
cards.downstream_use: Compare qualified clearance-scaling scenarios and preserve uncertainty; do not import a universal exponent or reference-compound parameter.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
